name: A game has pieces
statement: Every game is made of things that can be named and counted: boards, cards, tokens, players, scores.

questions.prompt: Name four things in Monopoly that you could list in a table.
questions.answer: For example: the 40 spaces, the players, each player's money, the property deeds and who owns them.

name: Templates
statement: A template is the general description of a kind of piece, the same in every game: a property card with its price and rent.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a template?
choices: It is the red player's turn

name: Instances
statement: An instance is one piece in one game, made from a template and carrying its own values: this Boardwalk, owned by red, with two houses.

questions.prompt: Two games of Monopoly are running at once. What do their Boardwalks share, and what can differ?
questions.answer: They share the template (price, rents); the owner and number of houses belong to each instance and can differ.

name: The state
statement: The game state is every instance's current values at one moment: enough to say exactly where the game stands.

questions.prompt: You photograph a chess board mid-game. What does the photo miss that the state needs?
questions.answer: Whose turn it is (and rules-relevant history such as castling rights); the photo shows positions only.

name: The view
statement: What the player sees is drawn from the state; two screens can draw the same state differently.

questions.prompt: In a card game, each player's screen shows a different hand. Is the state different for each player?
choices: Yes, each player has their own state
No, one state, drawn differently for each player
questions.answer: No, one state, drawn differently for each player

name: A save is the state
statement: A save file is the state written down; load it, draw the view again, and the game is back where it was.

questions.prompt: Why doesn't a save file need to store a picture of the screen?
questions.answer: The screen is drawn from the state, so storing the state is enough to draw it again.
